title: Apple is hiring engineers to build its own AI agent
slides: Apple wants its own AI agent — but why now?
It is hiring engineers specifically for agent systems
Apple has kept AI quieter than OpenAI and Google
Your iPhone could soon act without you tapping
Watch one Apple app for signs of an agent
thread_text:
1. Apple's AI agent hiring spree

Apple is hiring engineers specifically for agent systems, a clear signal it wants an AI that acts on your behalf — not just chats.

2. Why Apple stayed quiet

While OpenAI and Google raced to launch chatbots, Apple kept AI behind the scenes. That silence may have been strategy, not slowness.

3. Your iPhone without taps

Soon your phone could complete tasks on its own — booking, ordering, scheduling — without you touching the screen.

4. One app to watch

Apple's agent won't arrive as a standalone product. Look for it woven into an existing app you already use daily.

5. Are you ready to hand over control?

If your iPhone could act without you tapping, would you let it? Try listing three daily tasks you'd trust an agent to handle — then ask if Apple's timing makes sense.
